R8-A-audit-j5.body:
Read research/AGENT_TASKS/BRIEF_R8.md first. You are the adversarial auditor (Track 6). Deliverables, each with a verdict justified / gap / false and the exact line at fault:
1. Re-derive from the definitions, at N = 52: the identities (I1), Sum e_y = 14 - J, |D(u,v)| = c + #{y : u,v in M_y}, s(u,v) = 4|D| - c - 45 - E_both, Ex(u) formula, Sum_v s(u,v) = 2Ex(u). Then re-prove Lemma A at N = 52 (rounding modulo 4 at a vertex with j = 0, including the case of y with q_y in {7,8,9,10,11}). Then re-prove c(u,v) >= 1, stating every arc direction.
2. Audit research/N52_TIGHT_J_GE_6.md sections 1 and 2 line by line (the R4-C survivor kill and the J = 5, s = 5 hand proof, including the partition filter for heavy excess 9).
3. Audit the J <= 4 and s <= 3 parts: research/AGENT_TASKS/R1-C-n52-j-le-2.report.json (excluding J = 3 and J = 4) and research/AGENT_TASKS/R3-C-four-positive.report.json (s <= 3 at J >= 5). Either confirm each case or write a corrected argument for the case you find broken.
4. Read research/compute/n52_pairlevel.py and check that every constraint is a valid consequence of S_4 at N = 52 (variable domains included), and that the restriction of heavy miss-sets to V_+ is justified by Lemma A. List any row that is not justified.
Report status proved if the full chain J <= 5 impossible survives with your corrections, otherwise inconclusive with the precise gap. Write research/AGENT_TASKS/R8-A-audit-j5.report.json.

R8-A-audit-j5.title: Independent audit of the J <= 5 exclusion at order 52

R8-B-no-tight.body:
Read research/AGENT_TASKS/BRIEF_R8.md first. Branch: T has S_4 on 52 vertices and every pair has at least 12 dominators. Deliverables:
1. Prove: every in-degree is 25 or 26, exactly 26 of each (call them L and H); for v in L, T[N^-(v)] is 12-regular on 25 vertices, has S_3, and every pair inside it has at least 5 common in-neighbours inside it; for v in H, T[N^-(v)] has in-degrees 12 + eps with Sum eps = 13. Derive and prove the arc-count identities between L and H (for example, for w in L the number of out-neighbours in L plus the excess carried by its out-arcs into H equals 13; for w in H the excess on its out-arcs inside H equals its out-degree inside H). Check each identity by a short script on random tournaments where it is an identity, or explain why it is not.
2. Study a pair P = {a, v} with v in L and a -> v, so |D(P)| = 12 exactly. Let R = D(P) (12 vertices, T[R] min in-degree >= 5, T[R] has S_2 because the dominator of {a, v, x, y} must lie in R), O = the other 38 vertices. Write the analogues of (I1), Lemma I, s(u,v), Ex(u) and the rounding-mod-4 step for this 12-dominator pair (in-degrees inside R are 5 + t_x with Sum t_x = 6), and determine whether the pair-level system is infeasible, by hand or with a CP-SAT model in which T[R] is a variable 12-vertex tournament (min in-degree >= 5, S_2) and the degrees of R-vertices are 25 or 26. Every row must be a proved consequence; state each.
3. If that model is feasible, extract the surviving structure and try a contradiction from the 12-regular, S_3, pair-common-in-neighbour >= 5 tournament W = N^-(v) on 25 vertices (a Theorem-5-style identity inside W, or a count over all v in L simultaneously).
Status proved only for written proofs; solver verdicts are evidence. Write research/AGENT_TASKS/R8-B-no-tight.report.json.

R8-B-no-tight.title: Structure and exclusion attempt for the no-tight branch at order 52

R8-D-spectral.body:
Read research/AGENT_TASKS/BRIEF_R8.md and proof/F4_GE_52_HAND_PROOF.md section 3 first. Assume (as an input from research/N52_TIGHT_J_GE_6.md) that every tight pair at N = 52 has J >= 6. Deliverables:
1. Redo Corollary 2 at N = 52: a vertex v of in-degree 23 makes every {a,v} (a in N^-(v)) tight; derive the exact bound on Sum_{a in N^-(v)} e(a) and decide whether J >= 6 (or the per-pair-level facts in the brief) now excludes in-degree 23. Give the full argument.
2. Redo Corollary 3 at N = 52 for a vertex v with in-degree 24: the Gram matrix of the sets D({v,z}) has size 51, rank <= 24. Compute exactly how the off-diagonal row sum of a tight row (14 - J) compares with the diagonal, what threshold of J makes the tight block positive definite, and what bound on W_A = Sum_{x in N^-(v)} max(e(x),0) results. Then look for a strengthening valid for J in {6, 7, 8}: e.g. a weighted Gershgorin (scaling rows), a bound on the number of heavy outside vertices per tight row, use of exact M_{zz'} values from the tight-pair structure (entries are q_{z'} - 5 for z' outside R), or a second-moment bound on M. Prove whatever you claim.
3. Combine with the global budget at N = 52: Sum_v (d^-(v) - 25) = 26, |Z| <= 5, the in-degree of each vertex >= 23. Determine what the tight-pair branch then forces globally (how many tight pairs, which in-degrees), and whether any contradiction follows.
Write research/AGENT_TASKS/R8-D-spectral.report.json.

R8-D-spectral.title: Corollary 3 and global degree budget at order 52 with J >= 6

R8-E-independent.body:
Read research/AGENT_TASKS/BRIEF_R8.md first. Do NOT import research/compute/n52_pairlevel.py. Deliverables:
1. Implement from scratch a verifier of the statement 'no tight pair at N = 52 has J <= 5' at the pair level, using T[R] taken from the explicit list of the 551 5-regular S_2 tournaments on 11 vertices in proof/n51_local/reg11_S2.txt (one 55-character upper-triangle string per line, character k for pair (i,j), i<j in lexicographic order, '1' meaning i -> j). Verify first that the file really lists 551 pairwise non-isomorphic 5-regular S_2 tournaments, and if possible that it is complete (the number of 5-regular tournaments on 11 vertices up to isomorphism is 1223; you may cross-check with nauty/pynauty if available, otherwise with a canonical-form routine of your own). For each class and each placement of the j-vector (use automorphisms to cut placements; Lemma A forces every endpoint of a c = 4 pair into V_+), decide the pair-level system with c fixed by the class, using an exact method that does not rely on CP-SAT (for example your own branch-and-bound over heavy patterns and D-values, or HiGHS MILP with the final infeasibility re-checked by an exact rational Farkas certificate). Record counts and runtimes.
2. Produce checkable certificates in research/CERTIFICATES/ (create it): for each infeasible case either a Farkas multiplier vector over integer rows with a small checker script, or a case-split log that a separate 50-line checker replays. Write the checker as research/compute/r8e_check_certificates.py.
3. Validate the encoding on a case known to be feasible (with c >= 0 instead of c >= 1, J = 5 shape (2,1,1,1) must become feasible for some class/placement if R4-C is right; report what you find).
Write research/AGENT_TASKS/R8-E-independent.report.json.
R8-E-independent.relation_to_prior: research/compute/n52_pairlevel.py is one CP-SAT implementation without certificates. This builds a separate implementation with different variables and an independently checkable output.
R8-E-independent.title: Independent implementation and certificates for the J <= 5 exclusion

R8-F-asymptotic.body:
Read research/AGENT_TASKS/BRIEF_R8.md, proof/ERDOS902_PROOF.md sections 3-6, and the barrier notes it cites. Deliverables:
1. Identify precisely which inequality in Lemma 3.1 / Lemma 5.2 / the definition of a_j produces the constant c* = 0.7695..., and prove a statement of the form 'any argument using only the inequalities X, Y, Z cannot give a constant above c*' (state X, Y, Z exactly).
2. Use the structure that the method ignores: for |A| = s, T[D(A)] has property S_{n-s} (prove this), so |D(A)| >= f(n-s) and T[D(A)] itself satisfies every lemma recursively; also D(A) is undominated and has the in-degree structure of Lemma 1.3. Derive a recursion that uses f(n-s) (or the bounds on it) inside Lemma 3.1, and compute its limit constant numerically. Either prove an improved constant c' > c* rigorously (with a script verifying the numerics, research/compute/r8f_*.py), or prove that this extra structure provably cannot change the limit, and explain why.
3. On the upper side: state the best explicit upper-bound construction known to you (random tournaments, Paley, Graham-Spencer), check by computation for small n whether any explicit family (e.g. Paley or cyclotomic tournaments on primes p ~ c n^2 2^n with smaller c) beats ln 2 * n^2 2^n heuristically, and state precisely what is proved versus heuristic.
Do not claim the growth rate is determined. Write research/AGENT_TASKS/R8-F-asymptotic.report.json.
R8-F-asymptotic.relation_to_prior: The exhausted keys one-level-counting-past-cstar, two-stage-averaging-second-log and three-level-count-second-log concern adding counting levels. This task instead feeds structural properties of dominator sets (T[D(A)] has S_{n-|A|}) into the recursion, which those approaches did not use.
R8-F-asymptotic.title: Where the c* ceiling comes from and whether structure beats it

R8-G-construct.body:
Read research/AGENT_TASKS/BRIEF_R8.md first. You try to break the conjecture f(4) >= 53 and to improve f(4) <= 67. Deliverables:
1. Write a fast exact S_4 checker (C compiled with gcc if available, otherwise numpy bitsets) that counts undominated 4-sets and also reports the minimum number of dominators over pairs and triples. Validate it on the Paley tournament QR_67 (S_4) and QR_47, QR_59 (not S_4).
2. Run a local search (simulated annealing or tabu on arc reversals, cost = number of undominated 4-sets plus penalties for triples with < 5 dominators) on N = 52, seeded by (a) random tournaments with in-degrees 25/26, (b) QR_67 minus 15 vertices chosen to keep regularity, (c) doubly-regular-like circulants on Z_52 or Z_53 minus a vertex. Also run N = 60, 63, 66. Budget: at most 3 cores, at most 90 minutes total.
3. Report the best cost found per N with the tournament saved (research/compute/r8g_best_N.txt, adjacency rows), and the profile (min pair dominators, min triple dominators). If any tournament with S_4 on fewer than 67 vertices is found, verify it with a second independent checker and save it; that would be a counterexample candidate. A failure to find one is only weak evidence.
Write research/AGENT_TASKS/R8-G-construct.report.json.
R8-G-construct.relation_to_prior: R4-D excluded named algebraic families. This task runs targeted local search over general tournaments, seeded with the order-52 structure forced by the lower-bound analysis (score sequence 25/26), which no previous task did.
R8-G-construct.title: Adversarial search for S_4 tournaments on 52 to 66 vertices
